changelog: **External Correction — mixing your hand with the correction:** a new **Assist** slider (0–100 %) weights *only* the correction. Your own mouse movement always passes through at full sensitivity, so the feel and the DPI of your mouse never change with the setting — at 0 % you get pure pass-through, at 100 % the previous behaviour. A second control, **Hand priority** (counts/s, 0 = off), lets the correction step aside the faster you move: below the threshold it works at full strength, at the threshold it yields completely. The useful threshold depends on your mouse DPI, so the tab now shows your **hand speed live** — move the mouse the way you do in a fight, read the number, set the threshold just above it.

**External Correction — quadratic predictor (off by default):** estimates velocity and acceleration from the last three sender frames and extrapolates the aim error forward by *weight × the reported packet age* (**weight** 0–100 %). Measured: on smooth target motion it helps, on hard direction changes it overshoots the corner, and at weight 1.0 **all three algorithms become erratic** (error spikes of 50–80 px). If you try it, 0.5 is the sensible upper end. Left off, nothing changes.
**External Correction — "Reset to defaults" button:** puts *only* the External Correction sliders back to the firmware defaults. Your MIM spline settings are not touched.

**MIM splines — main switch** (MIM tab): splines are on by default and stay on unless you explicitly switch them off; the choice survives a restart. They no longer depend on the External Correction being active.

**External Correction rebuilt from scratch — three algorithms only.** **Adaptive**, **Jump** and **Robust** survive; "Classic" and "Snap" are gone and are now *rejected* instead of being silently remapped to a different algorithm. The rebuilt controller has no velocity estimator, no lead and no dead-reckoning, so "error = 0 ⇒ output = 0" is structurally true rather than merely intended. Its output is time-based, so it behaves the same whether the sender runs at 20, 48 or 120 Hz — the previous version was calibrated for 120 Hz and fell apart below roughly 86 Hz. The "signal is gone" gate now applies to *all* algorithms. The correction is **always off after a restart or a flash** and has to be enabled explicitly.

**New defaults, retuned against a realistic benchmark** (fluctuating 60–150 Hz frame rate, 16–26 ms latency jitter): **Reaching 30 → 40 ms**, **Jump 30 → 20 %**. The old values tracked a little closer but visibly shot past a target when it appeared (50 % overshoot, ~500 ms of ringing); the new ones halve that. Continuous tracking never oscillated at any setting — the overshoot was purely a target-acquisition transient.
**Reaching slider now steps in 1 ms** (was 10 ms). It is the sharpest lever on the control loop, and the useful range cannot be hit in 10 ms steps.

**Corrections above 127 counts inverted their sign (critical).** The USB mouse report carries dx/dy as a signed byte, so a 136-count correction silently became −120 and the aim ran *away* from the target instead of toward it (measured: 400 → 949 → 1369 px error). The telemetry showed healthy positive numbers because it logged them before the conversion. Outputs are now clamped. This affected **every** mouse output including the MIM splines, not just the External Correction.
